observed.facings.png: Three facings at one shared scale on a checkerboard. All show the same squat, six-legged arthropod. Its broad, flared carapace has scalloped plate margins, is brown and crust-textured, and is speckled with pale grey-green foliose lichen rosettes. South: a head-on view with a small broad head, two dark eyes, short clubbed antennae and a wide mouth pressed into a small lichen clump; jointed legs splay out on both sides. East: a side profile, with the low carapace running front to back, legs beneath, and the head at the right with an eye and clubbed antennae; the mouth is down in a lichen tuft. North: the rear of the carapace and splayed legs, with two antenna tips just showing above the far edge of the shell. No eyes or face are visible.
observed.south.png: Front view at full resolution: a wide, low lichen-crusted shell; a broad, flat head with two small dark eyes and short antennae; the mouth is lowered onto a small rounded pad of lichen. Six jointed legs splay widely. Painterly texture, with a thin dark outline.
observed.east.png: Side profile: an elongated, low carapace with a flared skirt rim and lichen rosettes on top. Jointed legs underneath. The head points right, with a dark eye and clubbed antennae, and the mouth sits in a lichen tuft at ground level. It reads clearly as a profile.
observed.north.png: Rear view: the back of the carapace, its scalloped rear margin, and splayed hind and mid legs. Two antenna clubs rise above the far (front) edge of the shell. There is no face and no eyes. The rear is a little more domed and the antennae add height.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human at max zoom, the creature is a small flat crust-coloured lump, about a third of a cell wide. At 32 px/cell it is a tiny grey-brown speck beside the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The south view shows the head head-on, with two eyes, antennae and a broad mouth facing the camera.

NORTH_REAR.seen: The north view shows the back of the shell and the hind legs. Only the antenna tips poke above the far rim; there are no eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three views are at the angled game camera, with legs and the shell skirt visible from the side. None is a plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: Body widths and shell sizes match across facings. The 28% height spread comes from the north antennae rising above the shell and the lower profile silhouette on east, so it is a matter of pose and silhouette, not a scale jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The lichen-crusted flared carapace, six jointed legs and clubbed antennae appear on all facings and turn with the body. The palette is consistent.

SIGNATURE.seen: It is clearly a tiny lichen-grazing crust creature: the shell is overgrown with lichen and the mouth is down on a lichen clump.

ALIEN.seen: It reads as an odd crust-coloured, lichen-shelled six-legged grazer with a turtle-like skirt. It does not look like a recognisable Earth weevil, because there is no snout and no glossy elytra, and most departures are present.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) It is tiny beside the human and hugs the ground, but no soil crust is drawn because a real-alpha sprite cannot show one. The low posture covers this line. Present. 2) There is a broad, low mouth on the lichen and no long snout. Present. 3) The body is low and wide with a flared skirt, though the shell centre is moderately domed. Mostly present. 4) Grazed lichen tufts sit at the mouth on south and east. Present, though small.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, with naturalistic texture and a thin dark outline. The eyes are small and dull, and nothing about it is cute or cel-shaded.

OURS.seen: This is a bespoke design, with no vanilla or other-mod donor resemblance.

ALPHA.seen: The cut-out is clean, with no ground patch or shadow. The only extra is the small lichen clump under the mouth on south and east, which is part of the grazing action rather than a backdrop.

SCALE.seen: At drawSize 0.5 it is a small creature beside the human, which fits a tiny grazer.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px it is a small grey-brown oval speck. It reads as a small critter, but detail is lost. That is acceptable for a creature this size.

request.prompt: A single tiny crustweevil, a lichen-grazing weevil at centimetre scale, in painterly vanilla RimWorld sprite style, realistic, with a clean dark outline, on a fully transparent background. The body is a flat, wide, shallow carapace like a thin lid laid on the ground. Its height is about a quarter of its width, the top is nearly level with only a gentle rise along the midline, and the rim skirts the surface. The shell is earthy brown-grey, with small patches of soil crust and pale grey-green lichen growing on its back, so it reads as part of the crust it grazes. The shell fills about 80% of the canvas width and sits centred. The head ends in a broad, flat, wide grazing mouth plate held at ground level, with a short blunt muzzle. The mouth plate grips one small tuft of pale grey-green lichen, a few centimetres of fronds lifted at the mouth and bitten off at the ends, so the tuft reads as food being eaten and belongs to the animal's own silhouette. Six short legs fold in along the edges of the shell in a walking pose, with short antennae at the head. The silhouette ends at the grazing mouthparts and the tuft they hold. The space beneath and around the body, legs, mouth and tuft is clean, empty, fully transparent, with the animal alone in the frame in the south, east and north views alike.

observed.facings.png: Three panels at one scale, each showing a swarm of about 80–100 small, flat, grey-brown, lens-shaped bodies. The swarm is densest and piled up at the bottom and thins into scattered single bodies toward the top, like a cloud lifting off the ground. Each body is a low, flattened oval or diamond carapace with fine radial ribbing and a fringe of short hair-like legs or bristles along one edge. South: the bodies are symmetric diamonds with a central seam, the fringe peeking out below. East: the bodies are longer side-on ovals with the fringe hanging under them, some tilted as if in motion. North: similar to south, with the leg fringe more visible below each body. No wings, eyes, antennae or bright markings anywhere. Clean checkerboard alpha.
observed.south.png: The south swarm alone: symmetric, diamond-to-lens grey carapaces with a ridge down the middle and bristly underside fringes. The cluster is denser at the base and scatters upward. No faces or eyes are drawn on any body. Monochrome dusty grey-taupe with soft painterly shading.
observed.east.png: The east swarm: the same grey bodies drawn as elongated side-on ovals, with the leg fringe trailing below and a few bodies angled as if rising. The palette and density match south.
observed.north.png: The north swarm: rounded grey carapaces seen from behind and a little above, with the fringe of legs along the lower edge more prominent. No eyes or face. Same density and palette as the other facings.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the swarm is a small grey speckle, about a third of a cell, on the dirt beside a human who stands about two cells tall. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a faint grey smudge, barely visible and nearly the colour of the ground.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South bodies are symmetric front-on diamonds with a central seam and the underside fringe toward the viewer. There are no faces on any facing, which suits faceless dust-coloured critters.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North bodies show the rounded rear and back with the leg fringe below. No eyes or face.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: Bodies are seen at the oblique game angle with their undersides and fringes visible. None is a flat plan view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured spread is 3%, and the swarms fill the same area on all three facings.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same grey ribbed carapace with a leg fringe appears in all three. On east the bodies turn to elongated side-on ovals, so the body turns with the facing.

SIGNATURE.seen: The defining 'hundred dustflutters up in one grey shiver' reads as a dense grey swarm lifting from a packed base into scattered bodies.

ALIEN.seen: Nobody would name a moth or butterfly. The flat ribbed lens bodies with bristle fringes look loosely like woodlice or trilobites, but as a rising swarm they read as an unfamiliar creature.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1) No broad veined wings anywhere: present. 2) Uniform dull ash-grey with no patterns, eyespots or markings: present. 3) Low, flat, ground-hugging carapaces: present. 4) Dense burst of many identical small bodies rising from the ground: present. 5) No feathery antennae or furry thorax: present.

STYLE.seen: Soft painterly shading with fine ribbing and no heavy keyline. No cute faces. The bodies are near-identical copies, which looks slightly repetitive but fits the 'identical bodies' departure.

OURS.seen: A bespoke swarm. Nothing like it exists in vanilla or common mods.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all facings. No ground patch, dust cloud backdrop or shadow under the swarm.

SCALE.seen: drawSize 0.3 makes the swarm a small speck beside the human. That fits tiny critters, though the burst could be larger to read as 'over your head'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell the swarm is a faint grey smudge almost the colour of the dirt and barely separable from the ground.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: There are no wings to fold, by design (departure 1).
